problem.name: Longest common substring of run-length encoded strings
problem.name_latex: Longest common substring of run-length encoded strings
problem.statement_latex: Given two run-length encoded strings with at most $n$ runs each and uncompressed length at most $N$, find a longest common substring. Let $d$ be the number of runs spanned by an optimal match, with the convention of Lee--Lin. Queries return a run character and length.
problem.statement_text: Given two run-length encoded strings with at most $n$ runs each and uncompressed length at most $N$, find a longest common substring. Let $d$ be the number of runs spanned by an optimal match, with the convention of Lee–Lin. Queries return a run character and length.

quantum.headline_latex: $\widetilde O(n^{2/3}d^{-1/6+o(1)}\operatorname{polylog}N)$ time by Lee--Lin; the algorithm searches over possible match scales.

classical.headline_latex: $O(n)$ encoded-input queries suffice to read the runs; classical compressed-string algorithms perform the remaining processing. This comparison measures oracle access rather than decompression time.
